title: Resilience, caching, and messaging — Module Quiz
description: Course assessment: Prevent duplicate charges when a dependency times out.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: A payment request times out. Does that prove the payment did not happen?
questions.explanation: The response may be lost after the operation succeeds.

questions.prompt: What makes a retry safe for a state-changing operation?

options.text: A random new payment id each time

questions.explanation: Repeated requests must not duplicate the intended effect.

questions.prompt: What does a circuit breaker do?

options.text: Temporarily stops calls after failure conditions

questions.explanation: It limits calls to an unhealthy dependency according to a policy.

questions.prompt: What must at-least-once message consumers expect?
questions.explanation: Duplicate handling is part of the consumer contract.

questions.prompt: Why store a processed marker and business effect in one transaction?

options.text: To avoid marking success without the effect or applying it twice after a partial commit

questions.explanation: Atomic recording connects deduplication to the effect.

questions.prompt: What does a cache TTL define?

options.text: How long an entry is considered usable under the cache policy
A guarantee the source never changes

questions.explanation: TTL is a freshness policy, not proof of current source data.
